_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 16:12:43Z)**_

The short answer: DeadReckon has built much of the hard execution kernel, but it has not yet delivered the complete original experience.

Today it is a serious local verified-run system. It is not yet a dependable “start this goal, walk away, and trust it to keep working until the goal is genuinely complete” product.

## Where the project stands

| Original promise | Current state | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Define “done” before starting | Plain English can be compiled into `acceptance.yaml`; an LLM critic looks for weak checks and goals a stub could satisfy | Strong, although users can still fall back to detected project tests instead of consciously approving a real contract |
| Run coding CLIs in isolation | Git worktree and copy isolation are mature; changes require deliberate promotion | Strong for source isolation |
| Keep running until the goal is met | A normal run is foreground and limited to 12 turns; recovery normally requires `resume`. Chain has detached execution; current uncommitted plan work adds orphan adoption | Major remaining gap |
| Independently judge completion | A separate gate runs deterministic checks and validates the completion marker | Strong deterministic floor, but not the semantic meta-judge described in the original vision |
| Resist a dishonest worker | The worker cannot bypass a failing test merely by claiming completion; tamper checks catch several forms of weakening | Useful protection, but current “cannot forge” language overstates the boundary |
| Capture the whole run | State, snapshots, events, traces, spend, provenance, implementation notes and reports are persisted | One of the strongest parts of the system |
| Make the experience pleasant | The default five-command interface is quite good | Internally, too many execution models and advanced commands still leak into the mental model |

The most important correction is about the judge. The LLM currently helps write and critique the definition of done in [acceptance.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/acceptance.rs:642). Final acceptance is then deterministic. There is no independent LLM reading the original goal, the resulting change and the evidence and deciding whether the goal was semantically achieved.

That means the original `/goal` idea is only partly present: semantic judgment happens before execution, not at the final boundary.

The current run loop also has a real ceiling: normal runs configure 12 turns in [run.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/commands/run.rs:496), after which the loop fails with a budget-exhausted state. State is durable, but the worker is not automatically durable. If its supervising process disappears, the job waits for an operator to resume or adopt it.

## What has genuinely been achieved

DeadReckon now has a credible “verified run” primitive:

1. Create an isolated workspace.
2. establish a completion contract;
3. run a chosen coding CLI;
4. retain state and evidence after every turn;
5. respond to gate failures with another corrective turn;
6. accept only after the external gate passes;
7. deliberately promote or export the result.

That is substantial. The current working tree passed the complete workspace test suite: 2,049 tests passed and none failed. I did not modify the repository.

The evidence system is also unusually thorough. [RunView](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/run_view.rs:20) gives a useful read model over persisted state and ledgers. The promotion boundary in [promotion.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:25) makes “completed” meaningfully different from “applied to my repository.”

So this is not a speculative pile of commands. It contains a real, tested kernel.

## Necessary complexity

These are inherent to the product and should remain:

- Safely isolating and later promoting source changes.
- Supporting different CLI providers and their different streaming, cancellation and accounting behaviour.
- Durable job identity, state, locking, recovery and cancellation.
- Compiling acceptance criteria into executable checks.
- A semantic judge for requirements that cannot be reduced to tests.
- Preventing the worker from modifying its own acceptance mechanism.
- Recording enough evidence to explain why a result was accepted.
- Scheduling dependent and parallel units of verified work.
- Explicit budgets, deadlines and blocked states. “Until done” must not mean “loop forever.”

## Incidental complexity

This is complexity created by the current shape of the implementation rather than the underlying problem:

- Forty-five top-level command variants, even though most are hidden from ordinary help.
- Several overlapping journey concepts: run, chain, plan/fork/merge, campaign, reshape and others.
- Control truth spread across state JSON, several JSONL ledgers and sidecar files, requiring hand-written reconciliation and orphan adoption.
- Repeated provider, retry, narration and budget policies in different orchestration layers.
- Multiple documentation and narration pipelines.
- Compatibility aliases, no-op flags and old spellings.
- Making implementation-note production part of the completion ritual, rather than deriving the after-state account from captured evidence.
- Continuing to deepen campaigns, learning, narration and other secondary systems before unattended goal execution is fully dependable.

The architectural smell is: there is one good verified-run atom, but too many ways to arrange and supervise it.

## The trust-boundary problem

The README’s “it can’t fake the finish” claim is stronger than the current implementation warrants.

The gate nonce is stored inside the run directory, and the marker uses Rust’s `DefaultHasher` in [gate.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/gate.rs:752), rather than a cryptographic MAC or signature. General CLI-provider and Bash-tool execution do not consistently deny access to gate material. In addition, automatic sandbox selection can fall back to no sandbox.

The system can truthfully say:

> A separate process runs the acceptance checks, and an existing completion marker cannot make failing checks pass.

It cannot yet universally say:

> A hostile coding agent is technically unable to forge acceptance.

Results should distinguish:

- `VERIFIED + CONFINED`
- `VERIFIED + UNCONFINED`
- `NEEDS REVIEW`
- `FAILED`

That would make the confidence claim precise rather than absolute.

## Where I would take it next

### 1. Finish the durable goal executor

Make `deadreckon start` create a durable local job, return its ID and detach by default. A small supervisor or user service should:

- lease pending jobs;
- recover abandoned leases;
- restart after terminal or machine failure;
- retain bounded retry, spend and time policies;
- distinguish blocked, cancelled, budget-exhausted and failed;
- supervise runs, chains and plans through the same scheduler.

Temporal is the useful exemplar here. Its core model is a durable execution reconstructed from an append-only event history, with explicit lifecycle operations such as start, describe, result, cancel, terminate and reset. DeadReckon should extract those durability and operator-semantics patterns without becoming a distributed workflow platform. [Temporal workflow execution](https://docs.temporal.io/workflow-execution), [Temporal CLI workflow commands](https://docs.temporal.io/cli/command-reference/workflow).

### 2. Restore the semantic meta-judge as a second key

Completion should require:

1. Deterministic checks pass.
2. An independent, read-only semantic judge assesses the goal, contract, diff and evidence.

The semantic judge must never override failed deterministic checks. It should return `achieved`, `revise` or `uncertain`, with evidence-backed reasons. If it is unavailable in strict mode, the result becomes `NEEDS REVIEW`, not accepted.

This is necessary complexity: natural-language goals cannot always be completely compiled into tests.

### 3. Close the gate boundary

- Keep signing material outside the agent-visible workspace.
- Use HMAC-SHA-256 or a proper signature.
- Deny gate and proof paths across every provider and tool route.
- Bind the receipt to the contract, policy, source revision and resulting revision.
- Fail closed for unattended trusted runs.
- Add adversarial tests in which an agent deliberately searches for and attempts to forge the marker.

### 4. Collapse the product around one job model

Keep the ordinary surface:

```text
start
attach
status
list
finish
```

Plans, chains and campaigns should become internal scheduling shapes or an explicitly advanced namespace. They should all create the same durable jobs and verified-run receipts.

Similarly, create one append-only control event history and derive current state and `RunView` from it. Rich spend, trace and documentation evidence can remain separate, but lifecycle truth should have one source.

### 5. Freeze secondary expansion and dogfood the promise

Temporarily freeze deeper campaign features, learning/improve surfaces and additional narration variants. Test the core promise on 20–30 real tasks across multiple repositories and providers.

Measure:

- unattended verified completion rate;
- automatic recovery rate;
- false acceptance and false rejection;
- number of operator interventions;
- time required to understand the final result;
- supervision and judging cost.

Kill the terminal, worker and machine during these trials. Remove network access. Attempt to tamper with the gate. Run DeadReckon on DeadReckon itself.

## Bottom line

DeadReckon contains a strong, unusually well-tested verified-run kernel inside an overgrown product.

The next phase should not be more orchestration features. It should make one promise completely true:

> Give DeadReckon a goal and an approved definition of done. It will work in isolation, survive interruptions, stop for explicit bounded reasons, independently verify both the checks and the meaning of the result, and leave behind a clear receipt explaining what happened.

Once that experience is reliable and pleasant, the plans, chains and campaigns become valuable multipliers instead of competing product models.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 16:12:43Z)**_

I’ll unpack “finish the durable goal executor” in concrete DeadReckon terms: what it means, what changes for the user, and what it does not require. I’m using the teaching skill because this is an architectural concept tied directly to this workspace.

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-07-29 16:12:43Z)**_

“Finish the durable goal executor” means making DeadReckon responsible for the job after the user starts it.

Right now, DeadReckon has durable records, but not fully durable execution.

## Today

A normal run behaves roughly like this:

```text
Your terminal
    ↓
deadreckon run
    ↓
coding CLI
    ↓
gate
```

The `deadreckon run` process is the supervisor. While that process is alive, it keeps giving the coding CLI turns and checking the result.

DeadReckon saves enough state to recover, but:

- closing the supervisor stops the work;
- restarting the computer stops the work;
- someone must run `resume`;
- a normal attempt stops after 12 turns;
- detached execution exists for chains, but is not the common execution model.

That is resumable execution: “we can pick up where we stopped.”

It is not yet durable execution: “DeadReckon continues to own the job until it reaches a legitimate stopping point.”

## The proposed experience

The user should be able to do this:

```bash
deadreckon start "Add password reset"
```

DeadReckon would:

1. Create the isolated workspace.
2. Prepare and approve the definition of done.
3. Record a durable job.
4. Return a run ID immediately.
5. Let a background supervisor carry on.

```text
Started run dr-4821
Workspace: isolated
Status: running
Attach: deadreckon attach dr-4821
```

The terminal is no longer responsible for keeping the work alive.

```text
Terminal                 DeadReckon supervisor
   │                              │
   ├── start goal ───────────────→│
   │←── run ID ───────────────────┤
   │                              ├── run coding CLI
   │                              ├── save evidence
   │                              ├── run gate
   │                              ├── retry if appropriate
   │                              └── finish or stop explicitly
   │
   └── may close safely
```

`attach` would only observe or interact with the job. Disconnecting would not stop it.

## What keeps it durable

The background supervisor needs four basic mechanisms.

### A durable queue

`start` writes the goal into a local queue before execution begins:

```text
Job: dr-4821
Goal: Add password reset
Contract: acceptance.yaml
State: queued
Budget: $20
Deadline: 4 hours
Workspace: /path/to/worktree
```

If no supervisor is currently running, DeadReckon starts one.

### Leases and heartbeats

When a supervisor takes a job, it records:

```text
dr-4821 is leased by process 9312 until 14:35:00
```

It renews that lease periodically.

If the process crashes, the lease expires. Another supervisor can safely adopt the job. This prevents both abandonment and two supervisors working the same job simultaneously.

The uncommitted plan changes currently in the repository are moving towards this kind of orphan adoption, but it should become a shared facility for every execution shape.

### Checkpoints after every important event

DeadReckon already persists much of this. The durable executor would formalize events such as:

```text
Job started
Turn 1 started
Turn 1 completed
Gate failed
Corrective turn requested
Turn 2 completed
Gate passed
Semantic judge passed
Run verified
```

After a crash, the replacement supervisor reads this history and knows what to do next. It does not start the entire job again.

### Explicit stopping reasons

“Keep running until done” should not mean infinite retries.

A job may stop because it is:

```text
VERIFIED
BLOCKED — requires user decision
BUDGET_EXHAUSTED
DEADLINE_REACHED
FAILED — unrecoverable error
CANCELLED
```

Those states are part of the confidence model. Quietly dying because a terminal closed is not.

## It does not require a large distributed system

This could initially be a small local service:

```text
deadreckond
```

On macOS it could run through `launchd`; Linux could use a user-level `systemd` service. DeadReckon could also begin with a simpler detached conductor process, provided it has leases and automatic adoption.

It does not need Kubernetes, a server database or a cloud account. SQLite or an append-only local event log would be sufficient.

## Why this is the highest-priority gap

The original promise is not primarily “we save excellent records.” It is:

> Give the system a goal and trust it to carry responsibility for reaching a verified conclusion.

Without a durable executor, the human still carries part of that responsibility:

- keeping the process alive;
- noticing that it stopped;
- deciding whether to resume;
- restarting orchestration after a crash.

With it, the human only intervenes when DeadReckon produces an intentional `BLOCKED` state.

A practical definition of done for this feature would include:

- Start a run and close the terminal: it continues.
- Kill the coding CLI: DeadReckon retries or records a clear failure.
- Kill the supervisor: another supervisor adopts the run.
- Restart the computer: unfinished jobs resume automatically.
- Never run the same turn twice concurrently.
- Respect spend, time and retry limits.
- Preserve the same run ID, workspace and evidence throughout.
- Finish only through the normal verification boundary.

That change would turn DeadReckon from a well-persisted foreground runner into the “start it and trust it” product described in the original goal.

+## Watchkeeper one durable Job and two-key completion 2026-07-29
+
+Watchkeeper makes guided `start` durable before the first agent turn. It
+freezes the approved goal, definition of done, policy, launch plan, source tree
+and revision under one Job ID. It then detaches a lease-fenced supervisor.
+`attach`, `status`, `list`, `kill`, `finish` and `report` resolve that Job
+without duplicating its backing run, plan or campaign.
+
+### Guided Jobs have 2 completion keys
+
+A contained native gate must pass the frozen deterministic checks. A fresh
+read-only semantic judge must then return `achieved`. The supervisor seals an
+HMAC-SHA-256 receipt that binds the authority, policy, launch plan, source and
+result revisions, tree digests, gate marker, judgment and confinement.
+
+A deterministic failure cannot be overruled. A Single Job can use semantic
+`revise` for another bounded worker turn. A Graph or Campaign parent records
+`revise` as `NEEDS_REVIEW`; safe parent repair is deferred. Uncertainty, judge
+failure, missing containment or an invalid receipt also stop
+`NEEDS_REVIEW`.
+
+### Graph and Campaign verify the parent result
+
+Guided review and full-plan work always uses at-end delivery. The supervisor
+copies the merged result into a same-ID parent run, runs its native gate, asks
+the semantic judge, validates the receipt and then promotes the parent.
+`finish` exports or applies that receipt-bound parent, not a mutable child
+artifact.
+
+A guided Campaign can recover an exactly linked persisted sub-plan. Before
+parent verification, it rebuilds the worst-of roll-up from current leaf
+evidence and compares it with the stored and merged copies. A refused or
+changed roll-up fails before the semantic judge. A clean campaign parent then
+uses the same gate, judgment, receipt and promotion sequence as a Graph.
+
+Direct `run`, `orchestrate`, `chain` and `campaign` remain process-owned
+compatibility paths. Guided automatic continuation refuses before starting
+work and prints the exact legacy `extend` command.
+
+### The worker cannot mint its proof
+
+Gate keys live outside the agent-visible workspace. Authority, lifecycle,
+gate, proof, snapshot, provenance and receipt paths are denied or read-only
+across the supported sandbox and provider routes. Version-2 markers and
+receipts fail closed on missing key material, synthetic proof,
+`sandbox_backend = none` or `contained = false`. Legacy runs retain their
+historical marker validator.
+
+### Service support is conditional
+
+`deadreckon supervisor install|start|status|stop` manages an owned per-user
+launchd or systemd definition. It pins the current binary, `DEADRECKON_HOME`
+and `PATH`, and refuses an unmanaged same-name unit. Repository tests cover the
+definitions and state classification. They do not prove an active service or a
+live reboot.
+
+The operator dogfood kit contains 24 tasks across 2 repository and provider
+slots. It also includes a metrics collector and human-review schema. Every task
+is `not_run`. This release does not claim live task rates, cross-provider
+results, machine-restart results, or false-accept and false-reject rates.

+def run_command(repo: Path, proof: ProofCommand) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    env["CARGO_TERM_COLOR"] = "never"
+    env["RUST_TEST_THREADS"] = "1"
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    completed = subprocess.run(
+        proof.argv,
+        cwd=repo,
+        env=env,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+        check=False,
+    )
+    elapsed = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
+    stdout = completed.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+    stderr = completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+    matching = [
+        line.strip()
+        for line in (stdout + "\n" + stderr).splitlines()
+        if proof.expected_test in line
+    ]
+    observed_pass = completed.returncode == 0 and any(
+        "ok" in line or "test result: ok" in line for line in matching
+    )
+    return {
+        "argv": list(proof.argv),
+        "returncode": completed.returncode,
+        "duration_seconds": elapsed,
+        "stdout_sha256": digest(completed.stdout),
+        "stderr_sha256": digest(completed.stderr),
+        "expected_test": proof.expected_test,
+        "matching_output": matching,
+        "observed_pass": observed_pass,
+    }
+
+
+def run_trial(repo: Path, trial: Trial) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if trial.macos_sandbox_required and (
+        platform.system() != "Darwin" or shutil.which("sandbox-exec") is None
+    ):
+        return {
+            "id": trial.trial_id,
+            "claim": trial.claim,
+            "proof_type": trial.proof_type,
+            "status": "unproven",
+            "reason": "the authoritative Seatbelt trial requires macOS sandbox-exec",
+            "limitation": trial.limitation,
+            "commands": [],
+        }
+    commands = [run_command(repo, command) for command in trial.commands]
+    passed = all(command["observed_pass"] for command in commands)
+    return {
+        "id": trial.trial_id,
+        "claim": trial.claim,
+        "proof_type": trial.proof_type,
+        "status": "passed" if passed else "failed",
+        "reason": None if passed else "one or more authoritative commands failed",
+        "limitation": trial.limitation,
+        "commands": commands,
+    }
+
+
+def git_value(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str | None:
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ("git", *args),
+        cwd=repo,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+        check=False,
+        text=True,
+    )
+    value = result.stdout.strip()
+    return value if result.returncode == 0 and value else None
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--repo",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2],
+        help="DeadReckon repository root",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--only",
+        action="append",
+        choices=[trial.trial_id for trial in TRIALS],
+        help="Run only one named credential-free trial; repeat for more",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    repo = args.repo.resolve()
+    selected = [
+        trial for trial in TRIALS if args.only is None or trial.trial_id in args.only
+    ]
+    trials = [run_trial(repo, trial) for trial in selected]
+    payload = {
+        "schema_version": 1,
+        "generated_at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
+        "credential_free": True,
+        "repository": {
+            "revision": git_value(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"),
+            "dirty": bool(git_value(repo, "status", "--porcelain")),
+        },
+        "host": {
+            "system": platform.system(),
+            "release": platform.release(),
+            "machine": platform.machine(),
+            "python": platform.python_version(),
+        },
+        "runner_sha256": digest(Path(__file__).read_bytes()),
+        "summary": {
+            "passed": sum(trial["status"] == "passed" for trial in trials),
+            "failed": sum(trial["status"] == "failed" for trial in trials),
+            "unproven": sum(trial["status"] == "unproven" for trial in trials)
+            + len(UNPROVEN),
+        },
+        "trials": trials,
+        "live_claims": list(UNPROVEN),
+        "matrix_status": "all_24_not_run",
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(
+        json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    print(args.output)
+    return 1 if any(trial["status"] == "failed" for trial in trials) else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
```

@@
 All 24 matrix entries start as `not_run`. A successful local test of the
 scripts does not imply that any provider trial ran.
+
+## Run the credential-free adversarial matrix
+
+The adversarial runner executes the repository's focused process, recovery,
+sandbox, receipt and delivery tests. It does not read provider credentials:
+
+```sh
+python3 examples/watchkeeper-dogfood/adversarial.py \
+  --output examples/watchkeeper-dogfood/credential-free-results.json
+```
+
+The JSON output records each command, duration, exit status, matched test line,
+and stdout/stderr digest. It labels proof by scope. A hermetic or local
+Seatbelt pass does not claim a live provider, another sandbox backend, an
+active user service, or a reboot.
+
+The following remain `unproven` in that file until an operator performs them:
+
+- worker death during an approved live provider run;
+- supervisor death during an approved live provider run;
+- host network loss during a live provider call;
+- a real machine reboot with the user service active;
+- a cross-provider hostile gate trial from the 24-task matrix.
```

+            "sha256:{}",
+            deadreckon_core::flight::sha256_file(&dogfood_dir().join("adversarial.py"))
+                .expect("runner digest")
+                .trim_start_matches("sha256:")

+    assert!(!live.is_empty());
+    assert!(
+        live.iter()
+            .all(|claim| claim["status"].as_str() == Some("unproven"))

        "reason": None if passed else "one or more authoritative commands failed",
        "limitation": trial.limitation,
        "commands": commands,
    }


def git_value(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str | None:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ("git", *args),
        cwd=repo,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        check=False,
        text=True,
    )
    value = result.stdout.strip()
    return value if result.returncode == 0 and value else None


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument(
        "--repo",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2],
        help="DeadReckon repository root",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--only",
        action="append",
        choices=[trial.trial_id for trial in TRIALS],
        help="Run only one named credential-free trial; repeat for more",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    repo = args.repo.resolve()
    selected = [
        trial for trial in TRIALS if args.only is None or trial.trial_id in args.only
    ]
    trials = [run_trial(repo, trial) for trial in selected]
    payload = {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "generated_at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "credential_free": True,
        "repository": {
            "revision": git_value(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"),
            "dirty": bool(git_value(repo, "status", "--porcelain")),
        },
        "host": {
            "system": platform.system(),
            "release": platform.release(),
            "machine": platform.machine(),
            "python": platform.python_version(),
        },
        "runner_sha256": digest(Path(__file__).read_bytes()),
        "summary": {
            "passed": sum(trial["status"] == "passed" for trial in trials),
            "failed": sum(trial["status"] == "failed" for trial in trials),
            "unproven": sum(trial["status"] == "unproven" for trial in trials)
            + len(UNPROVEN),
        },
        "trials": trials,
        "live_claims": list(UNPROVEN),
        "matrix_status": "all_24_not_run",
    }
    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.output.write_text(
        json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(args.output)
    return 1 if any(trial["status"] == "failed" for trial in trials) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

pub fn sha256_text(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(text.as_bytes());
    let digest = hasher.finalize();
    format_sha256(&digest)
}

pub fn sha256_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String> {
    let mut file = fs::File::open(path).with_path(path)?;
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    let mut buffer = [0_u8; 8192];
    loop {
        let read = file.read(&mut buffer).with_path(path)?;
        if read == 0 {
            break;
        }
        hasher.update(&buffer[..read]);
    }
    let digest = hasher.finalize();
    Ok(format_sha256(&digest))
}

            hasher.update(fingerprint.hash.as_bytes());

fn done_criteria_inspection_try_lines(selection: &setup::DoneCriteriaSelection) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    if let Some(path) = selection.path.as_ref() {
        lines.push(format!(
            "deadreckon def-done show --spec {}",
            path.display()
        ));
        lines.push(format!(
            "deadreckon def-done check --spec {}",
            path.display()
        ));
    } else {
        lines.push("deadreckon def-done show".to_string());
        lines.push("deadreckon def-done check".to_string());
    }
    lines.push("deadreckon def-done \"what should count as done\"".to_string());
    lines
}

fn done_criteria_prompt_detail(selection: &setup::DoneCriteriaSelection) -> String {
    let checks = selection
        .checks
        .map(|checks| format!("{checks} check(s)"))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
            "working directory exists, or cargo test when Cargo.toml is present".to_string()
        });
    match selection.path.as_ref() {
        Some(path) => format!("{} from {}", checks, path.display()),
        None => checks,
    }
}

fn apply_done_criteria_selection(
    decision: &mut StartLaunchDecision,
    source: StartDoneCriteriaSource,
    action: StartDoneAction,
    label: String,
    selection: &setup::DoneCriteriaSelection,
) -> Result<()> {
    decision.done_criteria_source = source;
    decision.done_action = action;
    decision.done_criteria_label = label;
    decision.done_contract = if selection.path.as_ref().is_some_and(|path| path.exists()) {
        commands::acceptance::compiled_contract_for_selection(selection)?
    } else {
        None
    };
    decision.done_divergence = decision
        .done_contract
        .as_ref()
        .map(|contract| commands::acceptance::reconcile(&decision.goal, contract));
    Ok(())
}

fn contract_review_try_lines(decision: &StartLaunchDecision) -> Vec<String> {
    vec![
        "deadreckon acceptance refine \"add a check that builds and runs the app\"".to_string(),
        format!(
            "deadreckon start \"{}\" --review-done",
            shell_display_quote(&decision.goal)
        ),
    ]
}

fn print_start_contract_divergence(decision: &StartLaunchDecision) {
    let Some(contract) = decision.done_contract.as_ref() else {
        return;
    };
    let divergence = decision.done_divergence.as_ref();
    if divergence.is_some_and(commands::acceptance::ContractDivergence::clean) {
        return;
    }
    println!("{}", ui_heading("done contract divergence"));
    commands::acceptance::print_compiled_contract(contract, divergence);
}

/// Replay a saved launch plan (C-P10): validate, re-clamp against the
/// current budget flag, stamp the resolution as a replay, and dispatch the
/// identical shape. The plan file is the decision — no classification, no
/// planning, at most the standard launch confirmation.
async fn start_replay_command(args: StartCommandArgs, plan_path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
    let mut plan = commands::course::load_launch_plan(plan_path)?;
    if plan.shape == commands::course::CourseShape::ChainExtend {
        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
            "a chain-extend plan cannot be replayed (it needs its parent run)",
            "deadreckon start \"<goal>\"",
        )));
    }
    if let (Some(cap), Some(ceiling)) = (args.max_spend, plan.budget.ceiling_usd)
        && ceiling > cap
    {
        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
            &format!("launch plan budget ${ceiling:.2} exceeds --max-spend ${cap:.2}"),
            &format!(
                "deadreckon start --plan {} --max-spend {ceiling:.0}",
                plan_path.display()
            ),
        )));
    }
    if args.max_spend.is_some() {
        plan.budget.ceiling_usd = args.max_spend;
    }
    plan.resolution.source = commands::course::ResolutionSource::Replay;
    plan.accepted_by = Some("replay".to_string());

    let mut decision = start_launch_decision(StartLaunchInput {
        goal: &plan.goal.clone(),
        requested_mode: match plan.shape {
            commands::course::CourseShape::Single | commands::course::CourseShape::ChainExtend => {
                crate::cli::CliStartMode::Run
            }
            commands::course::CourseShape::Plan => crate::cli::CliStartMode::FullPlan,
            commands::course::CourseShape::Campaign => crate::cli::CliStartMode::Auto,
        },
        stdin_is_tty: io::stdin().is_terminal(),
    });
    if plan.shape == commands::course::CourseShape::Campaign {
        decision.selected_mode = StartSelectedMode::Campaign;
        decision.selection_source = StartSelectionSource::ExplicitFlag;
    }
    decision.reason = format!("replayed launch plan from {}", plan_path.display());
    decision.child_count = plan.n;
    decision.provider_route = plan.providers.coder.clone();
    decision.planner_provider_route = plan.providers.planner.clone();
    decision.coder_provider_route = plan.providers.coder.clone();
    decision.reviewer_provider_route = plan.providers.reviewer.clone();
    decision.confirmed_by_start_picker = args.yes;
    let mut replay_args = args;
    replay_args.goal = plan.goal.clone();
    // Replays never prompt for setup; the plan is the decision. The accept
    // matrix still applies at dispatch (campaign guardrails included).
    resolve_start_setup(&mut decision, &replay_args, None, false)?;
    decision.child_count = plan.n;
    if let Some(recovery) = decision.recovery.as_ref() {
        let mut try_lines = recovery.try_lines.clone();
        try_lines.truncate(1);
        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
            &recovery.message,
            try_lines
                .first()
                .map(String::as_str)
                .unwrap_or("deadreckon try"),
        )));
    }
    materialize_start_done_criteria(&mut decision, None).await?;
    dispatch_start_command(replay_args, &decision, plan).await
}

                commands::orchestrate::recommend_child_count_for_goal(
                    &decision.goal,
                    CliPlanMode::FullPlan,
                )
            });
            let mut summary = format!("children={n}, planner={planner}, child={child}");
            if !decision.child_provider_overrides.is_empty() {
                summary.push_str(", overrides=");
                summary.push_str(&decision.child_provider_overrides.join(","));
            }
            Some(summary)
        }
        StartSelectedMode::Campaign => {
            let route = decision.provider_route.as_deref()?;
            let planner = decision.planner_provider_route.as_deref().unwrap_or(route);
            let child = decision.child_provider_route.as_deref().unwrap_or(route);
            let n = decision.child_count.unwrap_or_else(|| {
                commands::orchestrate::recommend_child_count_for_goal(
                    &decision.goal,
                    CliPlanMode::FullPlan,
                )
            });
            Some(format!("subs={n}, planner={planner}, child={child}"))
        }
    }
}

fn resolve_start_setup(
    decision: &mut StartLaunchDecision,
    args: &StartCommandArgs,
    prompter: Option<&mut dyn StartPrompter>,
    stdin_is_tty: bool,
) -> Result<()> {
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
    let defaults = config_defaults(&paths)?;
    if let Some(prompter) = prompter {
        resolve_start_provider(decision, args, &paths, &defaults, Some(&mut *prompter))?;
        if decision.recovery.is_some() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        resolve_start_orchestration_options(
            decision,
            args,
            &paths,
            &defaults,
            Some(&mut *prompter),
        )?;
        if decision.recovery.is_some() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
        resolve_start_done_criteria(decision, &cwd, Some(&mut *prompter), args.yes)?;
        if decision.recovery.is_none()
            && !matches!(
                decision.selected_mode,
                StartSelectedMode::Extend | StartSelectedMode::Campaign
            )
        {
            resolve_start_source_mode(
                decision,
                &paths,
                &cwd,
                Some(&mut *prompter),
                StartSourceModeRequest {
                    fresh: args.fresh,
                    worktree: args.worktree,
                    from: args.from.as_deref(),
                    allow_dirty: args.allow_dirty,
                    stdin_is_tty,
                },
            )?;
        }
    } else {
        resolve_start_provider(decision, args, &paths, &defaults, None)?;
        if decision.recovery.is_some() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        resolve_start_orchestration_options(decision, args, &paths, &defaults, None)?;
        if decision.recovery.is_some() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
        resolve_start_done_criteria(decision, &cwd, None, args.yes)?;
        if decision.recovery.is_none()
            && !matches!(
                decision.selected_mode,
                StartSelectedMode::Extend | StartSelectedMode::Campaign
            )
        {
            resolve_start_source_mode(
                decision,
                &paths,
                &cwd,
                None,
                StartSourceModeRequest {
                    fresh: args.fresh,
                    worktree: args.worktree,
                    from: args.from.as_deref(),
                    allow_dirty: args.allow_dirty,
                    stdin_is_tty,
                },

#[test]
fn start_dispatches_explicit_review_to_graph_job() {
    let temp = repo_tempdir();
    let repo = clean_git_repo(&temp);
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
    write_start_ready_setup(&paths, &repo);

    let output = deadreckon(&paths)
        .current_dir(&repo)
        .args([
            "start",
            "review through guided start",
            "--mode",
            "review",
            "--yes",
            "--quiet",
            "--plain",
        ])
        .output()
        .expect("start review dispatch");

    assert_success(&output);
    let root = only_job_root(&paths);
    let job: Value =
        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(root.join("job.json")).expect("job")).expect("job json");
    let plan = read_launch_plan(&root);
    assert_eq!(job["goal"], "review through guided start", "{job}");
    assert_eq!(job["shape"], "graph", "{job}");
    assert_eq!(plan["goal"], "review through guided start", "{plan}");
    assert_eq!(
        plan["signals"]["watchkeeper_driver"]["kind"], "review",
        "{plan}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        plan["signals"]["watchkeeper_driver"]["apply"], "at-end",
        "{plan}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn start_preview_json_has_next_actions_and_try_lines_without_ansi() {
    let temp = repo_tempdir();
    let repo = clean_git_repo(&temp);
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
    let empty_bin = temp.path().join("empty-bin");
    fs::create_dir_all(&empty_bin).expect("empty bin");

    let output = deadreckon(&paths)
        .current_dir(&repo)
        .env("PATH", &empty_bin)
        .args(["start", "json recovery", "--preview", "--json"])
        .output()
        .expect("start json preview");

    assert_success(&output);
    assert!(stderr(&output).is_empty(), "{}", stderr(&output));
    let out = stdout(&output);
    assert!(!out.contains("\u{1b}["), "{out}");
    assert!(!out.contains("Choose launch path"), "{out}");
    assert!(!out.contains("Choose provider"), "{out}");
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&out).expect("json");
    assert_eq!(value["kind"], "start");
    assert_eq!(value["will_start"], false);
    assert_eq!(value["try_lines"][0], "deadreckon try");
    assert_eq!(value["next_actions"][0], "deadreckon try");
    assert_eq!(value["primary_action"], "deadreckon try");
    assert_eq!(value["verdict"]["kind"], "blocked");
    assert_eq!(value["verdict"]["recommended_command"], "deadreckon try");
}

#[test]
fn detected_contract_asks_zero_questions() {
    // C-P8: Polyglot detection answers "done" — no prompt fires at all.
    let temp = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
    std::fs::write(temp.path().join("go.mod"), "module example.com/m\n").expect("write");
    let mut decision = start_launch_decision(StartLaunchInput {
        goal: "build the app",
        requested_mode: CliStartMode::Auto,
        stdin_is_tty: true,
    });
    let mut prompter = ScriptedStartPrompter::new(&[]);

    super::commands::start::resolve_start_done_criteria(
        &mut decision,
        temp.path(),
        Some(&mut prompter),
        false,
    )
    .expect("resolve");

    assert!(
        prompter.prompt_titles.is_empty(),
        "{:?}",
        prompter.prompt_titles
    );
    assert_eq!(
        decision.done_criteria_source,
        StartDoneCriteriaSource::Detected
    );
    assert_eq!(decision.done_action, StartDoneAction::DefaultGate);
    assert!(
        decision.done_criteria_label.contains("go test ./..."),
        "{}",
        decision.done_criteria_label
    );
    assert!(decision.done_criteria_label.contains("[detected]"));
}

#[test]
fn yes_flag_skips_question_and_carries_caveat() {
    // C-P8: --yes never asks; an unknown tree proceeds with the caveat on
    // the label (the gate surfaces it later — never a silent green).
    let temp = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
    let mut decision = start_launch_decision(StartLaunchInput {
        goal: "build the app",
        requested_mode: CliStartMode::Auto,
        stdin_is_tty: false,
    });

    super::commands::start::resolve_start_done_criteria(&mut decision, temp.path(), None, true)
        .expect("resolve");

    assert!(decision.recovery.is_none(), "yes proceeds, never refuses");
    assert_eq!(
        decision.done_criteria_source,
        StartDoneCriteriaSource::DefaultGate
    );
    assert!(
        decision.done_criteria_label.contains("caveat"),
        "{}",
        decision.done_criteria_label
    );

    // Without --yes the non-TTY refusal is unchanged (aligned with the
    // accept matrix: a script must opt in explicitly).
    let mut refused = start_launch_decision(StartLaunchInput {
        goal: "build the app",
        requested_mode: CliStartMode::Auto,
        stdin_is_tty: false,
    });
    super::commands::start::resolve_start_done_criteria(&mut refused, temp.path(), None, false)
        .expect("resolve");
    assert!(
        refused.recovery.is_some(),
        "non-TTY without yes still refuses"
    );
}
